entries.overview: A sturdy, flexible windpipe reinforced with C-shaped cartilage rings descending down the center of the neck.
entries.function: Provides an open airway linking the voice box to the main bronchi leading into the left and right lungs.

facts: Measures roughly 10 to 12 cm long and splits into the left and right main bronchi at the carina.
Incomplete cartilage rings keep the airway open while leaving soft muscle at the back so the esophagus can expand when swallowing.
Lined with tiny beating cilia that sweep trapped dust and mucus upward.

entries.overview: The primary airway branching leftward from the lower end of the trachea into the root of the left lung.
entries.function: Conducts inhaled and exhaled air between the windpipe and the lobar airways of the left lung.

facts: Passes underneath the aortic arch and is longer and slightly narrower than the right main bronchus.
Splits inside the left lung into superior and inferior lobar bronchi supplying its two lobes.

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Conducting Zone

entries.overview: The upper section of the left lung extending above the collarbone down across the front of the upper chest.
entries.function: Takes in inhaled air through millions of tiny alveoli where oxygen enters the blood and carbon dioxide leaves.

facts: Includes the cardiac notch along its front edge, leaving extra space inside the chest for the heart.
Separated from the left inferior lobe by a deep diagonal groove called the oblique fissure.

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Respiratory Zone

entries.overview: A wedge-shaped front-lower lobe found only on the right lung between its horizontal and oblique fissures.
entries.function: Expands during inhalation to perform gas exchange across delicate alveolar capillaries.

facts: Because the right lung has three lobes while the left has two, only the right lung contains a middle lobe.
Fed by the right middle lobar bronchus branching from the right main airway.

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Respiratory Zone

entries.overview: The large lower-back lobe of the right lung resting directly over the right dome of the diaphragm.
entries.function: Contributes major ventilated volume during deep breathing as the diaphragm pulls downward.

facts: Accounts for most of the posterior chest surface of the right lung.
Separated from the superior and middle lobes by the oblique fissure.

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — Respiratory Zone

entries.overview: A leaf-shaped flap of flexible cartilage behind the root of the tongue, at the top of the voice box.
entries.function: Folds down over the entrance to the windpipe during each swallow so food and drink go into the esophagus instead of the lungs.

facts: Composed of elastic cartilage attached anteriorly to the thyroid cartilage.
Acts as a directional valve keeping swallowed food and drink out of the lower airway.

entries.overview: The moist, blood-rich lining that covers the inside of the nose, including the curled shelves of the conchae.
entries.function: Warms, moistens and cleans the air you breathe in; its mucus traps dust and germs, and tiny hairs sweep that mucus toward the throat.

facts: Richly supplied with surface capillaries that warm cool inhaled air before it reaches the lungs.
Produces a sticky layer of mucus moved backward by microscopic cilia toward the pharynx.

sources.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e — The Nose and its Adjacent Structures

entries.overview: A short airway on the right side between the upper-lobe branch and the branches to the middle and lower lobes of the right lung.
entries.function: Carries air from the right main bronchus on to the middle and lower lobes of the right lung.

facts: Found only on the right lung, continuing below the take-off of the right superior lobar bronchus.
Splits into the right middle lobar bronchus and right inferior lobar bronchus.
